coverageGaps: No author-recommended Node major is stated in the bounded evidence; 24 is only CI-configured and 22.19.0 is the declared engines floor.

No exact pnpm version is pinned in the plugin repository: package.json has no packageManager field, and CI's pnpm/action-setup reads that field, so the development package-manager version is unpinned.

pnpm-workspace.yaml minimumReleaseAgeExclude entries use non-standard selectors (e.g. '@deepseek-ai/cosmokit@1.8.3 || 1.8.5') and are release-age policy rather than dependency overrides; they are not transferable to a consumer profile.
The devDependency '@types/node': '^26.6.3' is a type-definitions range and is not evidence of a supported Node 26 runtime.
Only the Web profile is documented by the plugin; no SDK, ACP, headless, or interactive TUI workflow is described in plugin-owned documents.
The DeepSeek balance capsule depends on the settings and credentials services plus an outbound /user/balance read; this authenticated integration is not exercised by a generic smoke check.
The compat seam matrix requires a dsh checkout (DSH_REPO) and fetched baseline tags, so it cannot run inside a generic isolated smoke check.
Disposable-profile install/uninstall verification is recorded as a manual per-release check, not an automated gate.
The browser half depends on the running harness serving the declared client seats and the packages listed in dsh.client.inject; a non-Web plane would not exercise the plugin UI.
The plugin's own pnpm workspace root and minimumReleaseAgeExclude policy are development-only and were not applied to any consumer profile.
recommendation.summary: dsh-context@0.60.0 is a DeepSeek Harness plugin whose manifest declares dsh.client.platform=web and whose README documents installation into the web profile ('dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-context') followed by 'dsh web'; no SDK, ACP, headless, or interactive TUI workflow is described by plugin-owned documents, so executionProfiles is web only. Node intent: engines.node is '^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0' in both the source and published manifests (declared-support for 22), and both CI workflows configure node-version '24' (ci-tested), which is the strongest available signal and therefore preferredNodeMajor 24; no author-recommended major was found. No exact pnpm version is pinned in the repository, so packageManagers is empty and the unpinned constraint is recorded as a gap. docs/compatibility.md carries three exact DSH baseline rows (0.1.5-rc.1, 0.1.7-rc.2, 0.2.0-rc.2), all declared compatible and each with a manual disposable-profile install/uninstall record; these are author claims, not Radar results. This recommendation is an environment inference only and does not establish compatibility.

conclusion.statement: dsh-context@0.60.0 (source commit 74117d8, artifact sha256 5f565b7f05d6f0f96a4c615e514ab710aff25425d0e7a87a7c19d53d6c675626) was exercised on Node 22 and Node 24 against three DSH baselines (0.1.5-rc.1, 0.1.7-rc.2, 0.2.0-rc.2). Launch finished with exitCode 0: 12 executed, 0 failed, 6 native cells, 6 surface cells, 0 adapter cells, 0 blocked, 0 deferred. Native: the 0.1.5-rc.1 cells on both Node majors are compatible (installed, registered, loaded, direct Node peer contracts satisfied); the 0.1.7-rc.2 and 0.2.0-rc.2 cells on both majors are unknown because dependency coverage is incomplete (4 missing Node peers each) - this is not a demonstrated runtime failure. Web surface: 0.2.0-rc.2 and 0.1.7-rc.2 are compatible on both Node majors with all nine stages passed (runtime, artifact, profile, install, registration, host, surface, interaction, shutdown), i.e. the Web host mounted and the declared plugin client entry was published, fetched, and materialized. The two 0.1.5-rc.1 Web cells (Node 22 and Node 24) are surface-incompatible: the DSH Web profile exited before exposing an HTTP surface because dsh-app-boot@0.1.5-rc.3 threw 'user patch-layer watching requires the Cordis HMR service' during profile boot; the plugin's own registration stage passed in both, so this is a harness-side boot failure on that baseline, not a plugin defect. No SDK or ACP adapter cells were scheduled, so no SDK/ACP plane was tested. These results are Radar observations on the stated baselines only and do not establish general consumer compatibility.

The two 0.1.5-rc.1 Web cells failed at harness boot (dsh-app-boot@0.1.5-rc.3 requires the Cordis HMR service) before any HTTP surface existed; the plugin's registration stage passed, so plugin-level Web behavior on that baseline remains unverified.

No exact pnpm version is pinned in the plugin repository, so the development package-manager version used by the author is unknown.
